title: Protocol for evaluating the abilities of diverse nitroaromatic prodrug metabolites to exit a model Gram negative bacterial vector
author: Chan-Hyams, Ackerley

steps.title: Prepare overnight bacterial cultures
steps.instruction: In sterile 15 mL centrifuge tubes inoculate 3 mL LBASG (LB + 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin, 50 µg mL⁻¹ spectinomycin, 0.2 % w/v glucose) with the nitroreductase‑expressing 7NT activator strain, the nitroreductase‑null 7NT control strain, and the SOS‑R4 recipient strain. Incubate 16 h at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.

steps.title: Inoculate day cultures and induce expression
steps.instruction: The following morning verify turbidity (OD₆₀₀ > 2.5 if measured). Transfer 0.5 mL of each overnight culture into 10 mL LBASGI (LBASG + 50 µM IPTG) in separate tubes. Incubate 3 h at 30 °C, 200 rpm. Dilute each culture with fresh LBASGI to an OD₆₀₀ of 0.8 before prodrug challenge.

steps.title: Add control and challenge media to plate
steps.instruction: In a 384‑well microtitre plate add 30 µL of control media (LBASGI only) or 30 µL of challenge media (LBASGI supplemented with twice the desired final prodrug concentration) to each well. Dispense 60 µL of sterile media into the wells surrounding the experimental wells to act as a protective barrier.

steps.title: Dispense co‑cultures at desired ratios
steps.instruction:
For each activator:recipient ratio prepare the appropriate mixture and add to the wells:
• 50:50 ratio – pipette 15 µL of the 7NT activator day culture (or 7NT null control) and 15 µL of the SOS‑R4 recipient day culture into each assigned well (final volume 60 µL).
• 10:90 ratio – in a 1.5 mL tube mix 100 µL of the 7NT activator (or 7NT null) with 900 µL of the SOS‑R4 recipient culture, vortex to mix, then dispense 30 µL of this mixture into each assigned well (final volume 60 µL).
For each strain also set up replicate wells in both control and challenge media to determine background growth inhibition and GFP expression.

steps.title: Mix, record OD, incubate, and read fluorescence
steps.instruction: After all cultures are added, mix each well by pipetting. Record the OD₆₀₀ of every experimental well using a microplate photometer. Incubate the plate at 30 °C, 200 rpm for 3.5 h. Then record OD₆₀₀ and GFP fluorescence (excitation 490 nm, emission 530 nm) on the same microplate reader.

steps.title: Calculate fluorescence fold change and inhibition
steps.instruction: For each prodrug condition compute the mean GFP fluorescence of the technical replicates for the Test condition and divide by the mean of the corresponding Control condition to obtain the fold increase. Assess growth inhibition by comparing OD₆₀₀ of prodrug‑challenged versus unchallenged wells; inhibition must not exceed 20 %.

steps.title: Pool technical replicates for cytometry
steps.instruction: For every challenge condition pool the 30 µL technical replicate wells from the microtitre plate into individual 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. Also pool the negative‑control (no prodrug) and positive‑control (prodrug‑challenged) strains for later flow‑cytometer gating.

steps.title: Prepare PBS tubes for cytometry
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 mL of filter‑sterilized PBS (pH 7.4) into each 14 mL round‑bottom polypropylene tube (or the tube type compatible with your flow cytometer).

steps.title: Set cytometer gates using controls
steps.instruction: Set the flow cytometer to the lowest flow rate (~12 µL min⁻¹). Load 25 µL of the pooled negative‑control sample into a PBS tube, vortex 5 s, and begin collection to define background FSC/SSC and GFP fluorescence; adjust the selection gate just above this baseline. Then load 25 µL of the pooled positive‑control (prodrug‑challenged) sample, vortex 5 s, and raise the GFP gate upper limit until the highest expected fluorescence is captured. Record instrument settings (e.g., on a BD FACSCanto II: FSC 570, SSC 450, GFP 555).

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence data for each condition
steps.instruction: For each pooled test or control sample add 25 µL to a PBS tube, vortex 5 s, and acquire 30,000 fluorescent events within the established gate at low flow rate. Perform three technical replicates per condition by repeating the 25 µL addition and acquisition three times. Monitor the proportion of events outside the gate; if high, readjust gate boundaries.

steps.title: Process cytometry data and compute fold differences
steps.instruction: Export the data and record the GFP geometric mean for each technical replicate using Flowing Software v2.5.1 or FlowJo. For each biological replicate calculate the fold difference: average geometric mean of Test replicates ÷ average geometric mean of Control replicates. Values significantly >1 indicate activation of fluorescence in the recipient population due to the by‑stander effect. Perform at least three biological replicates (independent overnight cultures) for each prodrug tested.
